title: Transforming Arrays
learning_outcomes: Explain what transforming arrays contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: array_map().
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: PHP arrays are ordered maps that can represent lists, keyed records, and nested collections. Keys, missing values, sorting, and transformation order all affect the resulting data. In this lesson, focus on array_map(); then compare it with array_filter(). Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use transforming arrays when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Transforming Arrays
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$values = [1, 2, 3];
$doubled = array_map(static fn (int $n): int => $n * 2, $values);
echo implode(",", $doubled) . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
